text: dsh-pro-standards 是一个面向 DSH 编码助手的技能插件包，通过 Cordis bundle 挂载入口，并将包内技能注册到 DSH 的技能服务。技能要求助手在修改项目、安装依赖、调用接口或整理文件前，查找适用规范，结合项目场景判断采用官方要求还是行业惯例，再检查计划与规范的差距；有差距时说明理由并给出提醒。技能还提供按需查阅的项目结构、依赖、代码、文档、测试、版本和开源流程细则。适合希望编码助手在实际开发任务中遵循项目约定、解释取舍并减少不合场景操作的用户。代码没有要求 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-pro-standards registers bundled guidance as a DSH skill. Before project changes, it prompts a coding assistant to find standards, consider context, and explain gaps. Topics include project structure, dependencies, code, docs, tests, and releases. No API key or external service is required.
希望编码助手动手改项目之前，先核对项目约定和合适的行业做法。
让 DSH 在安装依赖或整理文件前先检查做法是否符合项目规范。
I want my coding assistant to check project conventions before changing files or adding dependencies.
dsh-pro-standards 的功能「项目操作前的规范判断」：引导编码助手在留下项目改动前先找适用标准、结合场景判断取舍并检查差距。通过 DSH 加载该技能后，可在开发任务中自动触发，也可由用户直接要求按规范检查改动。

dsh-pro-standards README · dsh-pro-standards · 专业规范守则：**中文** | [English](README.en.md)

一个 DSH 插件包（bundle），内含同名技能：让 AI 编码助手动手之前先按专业从业者的方式想一遍——**正规做法是什么、当前场景该跟哪一边、我和它差在哪**——再决定怎么做。

dsh-pro-standards README · 它解决什么问题：AI 助手最容易出的问题，往往不是「不会写」，而是「不看场合就写」：

- 项目已有 `pnpm-lock.yaml`，它顺手 `npm install`，锁文件乱了；
- 一次性脚本的依赖被写进正式 manifest，越堆越重；
- 参数凭记忆编，跑起来才发现接口对不上；
- 目录里十几个同类型的散文件，没人知道哪个是入口；
- 做完不说改了啥，也不留回滚点。

`dsh-pro-standards` 做的事，是在这类动作**之前**插一段判断，而不是事后补救。

dsh-pro-standards README · 核心方法：三步判断：任何会给项目留下痕迹的操作（装依赖、调接口、写代码、组织文件、提交发布、写文档……）之前，走三步：

| 步骤 | 问什么 | 落到哪 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 找标准 | 这件事的「正规做法」是什么？ | 官方文档 / 项目现有约定（AGENTS.md、README、lockfile、代码风格）/ 行业惯例 |
| 2 看场景 | 该跟官方还是跟行业？ | 临时随用、行业普遍 → 行业惯例；长期复用、团队协作、安全相关、官方强制 → 官方规范 |
| 3 查差距 | 我的做法和标准差在哪？ | 有差距就按模板提醒；没差距就安静做事 |

三条总原则：

1. **情境化取舍**，不做规则复读机；
2. **说出理由**，每个取舍附一句为什么；
3. **提醒式，不硬拦**——讲清后果和正规做法，你坚持原样也放行，只留一句风险提示。

拿不准的时候，它应该停下来问你，而不是替你猜。

dsh-pro-standards README · 怎么装：**方式一：作为 DSH 插件包安装（推荐）**

`package.json` 里声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，安装后自动挂载 `index.js`，把自带的 `skills/` 注册进 dsh 的技能目录，不需要手动复制。

**从 GitHub 安装（现在就能用）**——先克隆，再把克隆下来的目录作为本地包装进去：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile 名> add link:./dsh-pro-standards
```

Windows PowerShell（路径用绝对路径更稳）：

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile 名> add link:C:\你的路径\dsh-pro-standards
```

dsh-pro-standards README · 怎么装：**从 npm 安装**（最省事；具体版本以 npm 上为准）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile 名> add dsh-pro-standards
```

装好后技能列表里会出现 `dsh-pro-standards`，插件详情里能看到标题、描述和图标。改 `index.js` 后不会热重载，把插件关掉再打开即可生效。

**方式二：只复制技能（不装插件）**

效果一样能用，只是没有插件清单和图标。**与方式一二者择一**——两种都装会出现同名两份技能。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills/dsh-pro-standards
cp -r dsh-pro-standards/skills/dsh-pro-standards/. ~/.dsh/skills/dsh-pro-standards/
```

dsh-pro-standards README · 怎么装：```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$HOME\.dsh\skills\dsh-pro-standards" | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Recurse .\dsh-pro-standards\skills\dsh-pro-standards\* "$HOME\.dsh\skills\dsh-pro-standards"
```

| 运行时 | 技能目录 |
|---|---|
| DSH（DeepSeek Harness） | `~/.dsh/skills/`（跨运行时别名 `~/.agents/skills/`） |

建议目录名与 `SKILL.md` 里的 `name` 字段保持一致（`dsh-pro-standards`）：运行时是按 frontmatter 的 `name` 识别技能的，目录同名只是方便对照、不容易弄错。

dsh-pro-standards README · 怎么用：两种触发方式：

- **自动**：如果你的 agent 规则里配了「技能路由」条款（命中开发、装依赖、组织文件、写文档这类任务时先加载匹配的技能），它会随规则一起被加载；
- **手动**：直接说——「用 dsh-pro-standards 检查一下这个项目」「按规范看看这次改动」。

dsh-pro-standards README · 什么时候会用到它：技能目录每轮都在模型的上下文里（只有名字和一句描述），**要不要加载由模型自己判断**。下面这些任务命中率最高：

| 会用到 | 不会用到 |
|---|---|
| 新建项目、定目录结构、决定该建哪些文件 | 闲聊、纯问答（「这个函数什么意思」） |
| 决定什么进仓库、什么该忽略 | 写一段独立的代码片段 |
| 装依赖、选包管理器 | 纯计算、查资料 |
| 整理散乱文件、判断该放哪个目录 | 模型判断「这活儿太小，犯不着」 |
| 写 README、更新 CHANGELOG | |
| 准备开源、发版、打 tag | |

想提高命中率有两个抓手：把「技能路由」写进 agent 规则（命中开发类任务先加载技能），或者直接点名——「用 dsh-pro-standards 看看这个项目」。

注意命中之后只加载入口（约 3.8 KB），具体细则再按索引读，不会一次全灌进上下文。

一次典型的对话：

dsh-pro-standards README · 什么时候会用到它：> **你**：帮我装个命令行工具，直接 curl 下载二进制就行。
>
> **助手**：⚠️ 这不太合规：直接下载二进制丢进 PATH。
> 麻烦是：没有版本管理、升级要手动、来源也难验证。
> 正规做法是：用包管理器装，比如 `npm i -g <pkg>`，或者项目内 `pnpm add -D <pkg>`。
> 要按正规的来吗？（你坚持原样也 OK）

dsh-pro-standards README · 它怎么接进 DSH：`cordis.patch.yml` 插入一行插件，挂载 `index.js`。`index.js` 在 `apply` 时读取 `skills/` 下每个 `SKILL.md`，用 `skills` 服务**公开的** `register()` 接口注册成运行时技能，并把技能目录作为 `resourceBase`——所以 `references/` 里的相对引用能正常解析。

正文在插件挂载时读入一次，升级后重新挂载即刷新。整个插件不依赖任何 dsh 内部包，只用到 `skills` 这一项公开服务。

dsh-pro-standards README · 目录结构：```
dsh-pro-standards/
├── index.js                 # 插件入口：把 skills/ 注册进 dsh 技能目录
├── cordis.patch.yml         # bundle 补丁：安装后挂载 index.js
├── skills/

`SKILL.md` 是入口（约 4.5 KB），自带完整的三步判断与提醒模板，末尾一张索引表指向 `references/` 下的 13 份细则——仓库骨架、忽略规则、依赖安装、接口调用、代码规范、文件结构、开源流程、文档规范、版本与发布、测试与 CI、GitHub 平台约定、发布后维护，以及通用判断框架与话术。每份独立完整，**只读用到的那一份**。
dsh-pro-standards README · 为什么不做穷举清单：清单永远追不上场景，还会过期。这个技能只给**一套判断方法**，具体细则按需展开：`SKILL.md` 保持精简，常驻上下文成本低；细则放在 `references/` 里，只在需要时读。

dsh-pro-standards README · dsh-pro-standards · Professional Standards：[中文](README.md) | **English**

A DSH bundle that ships a skill of the same name: before touching a project, an AI coding agent thinks the way a competent practitioner does — **what is the proper way to do this, should this situation follow the official rule or the industry norm, and where does my plan differ** — then acts.
dsh-pro-standards README · The problem it solves：The most common failure of an AI coding agent is not "it cannot write code". It is "it writes without looking at the situation":
dsh-pro-standards README · The problem it solves：`dsh-pro-standards` inserts a short judgement step **before** such actions, instead of cleaning up afterwards.

dsh-pro-standards README · Core method: the three-step check：Before any action that leaves a mark on the project (installing dependencies, calling an API, writing code, organising files, committing, releasing, writing docs), take three steps:

dsh-pro-standards README · Core method: the three-step check：| Step | Question | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Find the standard | What is the proper way to do this? | Official docs / existing project conventions (AGENTS.md, README, lockfile, code style) / industry norms |
| 2 Read the situation | Should this follow the official rule or the industry norm? | One-off or widespread-in-the-industry → industry norm; long-lived, collaborative, security-related, or officially mandated → the official rule |
| 3 Check the gap | How does my plan differ from the standard? | If there is a gap, raise it with the template; if not, just do the work |

dsh-pro-standards README · Install：**Option 1: install it as a DSH bundle (recommended)**

`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so installing it mounts `index.js`, which registers the bundled `skills/` tree into dsh's skill catalog. No manual copying needed.

**Install from GitHub (works today)** — clone it, then install the cloned directory as a local package:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add link:./dsh-pro-standards
```

dsh-pro-standards README · Install：Windows PowerShell (an absolute path is more reliable):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add link:C:\your\path\dsh-pro-standards
```

**Install from npm** (the easiest route; npm carries the released version):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add dsh-pro-standards
```

dsh-pro-standards README · Install：After installing, `dsh-pro-standards` shows up in the skill list, with its title, description and icon visible in the plugin details. Edits to `index.js` are not hot-reloaded — disable and re-enable the plugin to apply them.

**Option 2: copy only the skill (no plugin)**

Same skill, no plugin manifest or icon. **Pick one of the two options** — installing both yields two skills with the same name.

dsh-pro-standards README · Install：```bash
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills/dsh-pro-standards
cp -r dsh-pro-standards/skills/dsh-pro-standards/. ~/.dsh/skills/dsh-pro-standards/
```

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WhichWitchWin/dsh-pro-standards.git
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$HOME\.dsh\skills\dsh-pro-standards" | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Recurse .\dsh-pro-standards\skills\dsh-pro-standards\* "$HOME\.dsh\skills\dsh-pro-standards"
```

dsh-pro-standards README · Install：| Runtime | Skills directory |
|---|---|
| DSH (DeepSeek Harness) | `~/.dsh/skills/` (cross-runtime alias `~/.agents/skills/`) |

Keep the directory name the same as the `name` field in `SKILL.md` (`dsh-pro-standards`): the runtime identifies a skill by the frontmatter `name`, so a matching directory name merely keeps the two from drifting apart.

dsh-pro-standards README · When it gets used：The skill catalog is present in the model's context on every turn (name plus a one-line description only); **the model decides whether to load it**. These tasks hit most often:

dsh-pro-standards README · When it gets used：| Loaded for | Not loaded for |
|---|---|
| Starting a project, choosing a directory layout, deciding which files to create | Small talk, plain Q&A ("what does this function do") |
| Deciding what belongs in the repo and what to ignore | Writing a standalone code snippet |
| Installing dependencies, choosing a package manager | Pure computation, looking things up |
| Tidying scattered files, deciding where something goes | The model judging the task too small to bother |
| Writing a README, updating a CHANGELOG | |
| Preparing to open-source, releasing, tagging | |

dsh-pro-standards README · When it gets used：Two levers raise the hit rate: put a routing clause in your agent rules (load the matching skill before development tasks), or name it directly — "check this project with dsh-pro-standards".

Note that a hit only loads the entry point (about 3.8 KB); the detailed files are read by index, so nothing is dumped into context wholesale.

A typical exchange:

dsh-pro-standards README · When it gets used：> **You**: Just install that CLI tool — `curl` the binary and drop it in PATH.
>
> **Agent**: ⚠️ That is not quite proper: dropping a downloaded binary into PATH.
> The trouble: no version management, manual upgrades, and the source is hard to verify.
> The proper way: install it with a package manager, e.g. `npm i -g <pkg>`, or `pnpm add -D <pkg>` inside the project.
> Do it the proper way? (Your call — the original approach is fine too.)

dsh-pro-standards README · How it plugs into DSH：`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one plugin row that mounts `index.js`. During `apply`, it reads every `SKILL.md` under `skills/` and registers each one as a runtime skill through the **public** `register()` method of the `skills` service, using the skill directory as its `resourceBase` — so relative references such as `references/` resolve correctly.

dsh-pro-standards README · How it plugs into DSH：The body is read once when the plugin mounts; upgrading the package remounts it, picking up the new text. The plugin depends on no dsh-internal package, only on the public `skills` service.

dsh-pro-standards README · Repository layout：```
dsh-pro-standards/
├── index.js                 # Plugin entry: registers skills/ into dsh
├── cordis.patch.yml         # Bundle patch: mounts index.js on install
├── skills/

dsh-pro-standards README · Repository layout：`SKILL.md` is the entry point (about 4.5 KB) and works on its own: three-step check, principles, reminder template, then an index table pointing at thirteen files under `references/` — repository skeleton, ignore rules, dependency installation, API usage, code style, file layout, open-source workflow, documentation, versioning and release, testing and CI, GitHub conventions, post-release maintenance, plus the judgement framework and wording. Each file stands alone; **read only the one you need**.

dsh-pro-standards README · Why there is no exhaustive checklist：A checklist never catches up with reality, and it goes stale. This skill ships **one method** and expands the detail on demand: `SKILL.md` stays small so it costs little context, while the detail lives in `references/` and is read only when needed.
section: Why there is no exhaustive checklist
